You are a senior full-stack SaaS engineer and AI architect.

Your task is to design and generate a production-ready MICRO-SAAS WEB APPLICATION
called “AskCSV AI”.

-----------------------
PRODUCT GOAL
-----------------------
Build a web application where:
1. A user uploads a CSV or Excel file
2. The system automatically detects columns and data types
3. The user asks questions about the data in plain English
4. AI converts the question into SAFE, READ-ONLY SQL
5. The system executes the query on the uploaded data
6. The filtered result is shown in a table preview
7. The user can download the filtered data (CSV / Excel)

No SQL knowledge required by the user.

-----------------------
CORE FEATURES (MVP ONLY)
-----------------------
• File upload (CSV, XLSX)
• Auto schema detection
• Column preview (first 10 rows)
• Natural language → SQL conversion
• Query explanation before execution
• Result preview table
• Download filtered data
• Auto-delete uploaded files after 24 hours
• Read-only queries only (SELECT)

-----------------------
TECH STACK (STRICT)
-----------------------
Frontend:
• Next.js
• Tailwind CSS
• TanStack Table

Backend:
• Node.js
• Express
• Multer for uploads
• DuckDB for query execution

AI:
• Gemini API
• Prompt-based SQL generation

-----------------------
AI RULES (CRITICAL)
-----------------------
The AI must:
• Generate ONLY SELECT queries
• Use ONLY provided table schema
• Never modify, delete, or update data
• Ask clarification questions if the query is ambiguous
• Explain the query in simple English
• Reject invalid or unsafe queries

-----------------------
SYSTEM PROMPT FOR SQL GENERATION
-----------------------
"You are a data query assistant.
Convert user questions into SAFE, READ-ONLY SQL queries.
Use ONLY the provided schema.
If the question is ambiguous, ask for clarification.
Output ONLY valid SQL.
Table name: uploaded_data."

-----------------------
USER FLOW
-----------------------
1. Upload file
2. Show detected columns + sample rows
3. Input question box
4. Show query explanation
5. Show result preview
6. Enable download buttons

-----------------------
SCALABILITY & PERFORMANCE
-----------------------
• Handle up to 1000 concurrent users
• Limit file size (configurable)
• Queue long queries
• Stateless backend design

-----------------------
SECURITY & TRUST
-----------------------
• Temporary file storage
• Auto cleanup after 24 hours
• No data used for AI training
• SQL injection protection
• Read-only enforcement

-----------------------
OUTPUT EXPECTATION
-----------------------
Generate:
1. Clean folder structure
2. Backend API endpoints
3. Frontend pages & components
4. AI prompt integration logic
5. Query validation logic
6. Download file logic

Do NOT include unnecessary features.
Focus on clarity, simplicity, and reliability.

### 1. Prerequisites
Ensure you have [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) installed on your computer.

### 2. Project Setup
Open your terminal or command prompt and run the following commands:

```bash
# Create a new directory
mkdir askdata-ai
cd askdata-ai

# Initialize a npm project
npm init -y

# Install necessary dependencies
npm install react react-dom @google/genai
npm install -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react typescript
```

### 3. Create the Project Structure
Inside the `askdata-ai` folder, create the files as provided in the code. Your folder structure should look like this:

```text
askdata-ai/
├── index.html
├── index.tsx
├── App.tsx
```

### 4. Create `vite.config.ts`
Vite needs a small configuration file to understand how to handle React and the Gemini API key. Create a file named `vite.config.ts` in the root folder:

```typescript
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  define: {
    // This allows the app to access your API key
    'process.env.API_KEY': JSON.stringify(process.env.VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY)
  }
});
```

### 5. Adjusting `index.html` for Local Use

```html
<!-- Replace the existing script tag with this -->
<script type="module" src="/index.tsx"></script>
```

### 6. Run the Application
To run the app, you need to provide your Google Gemini API Key. You can get one for free at [ai.google.dev](https://ai.google.dev/).

Run this command in your terminal:

```bash
# For Windows (Command Prompt)
set VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY=your_actual_key_here && npx vite

# For Mac/Linux or Windows (PowerShell)
$env:VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY="your_actual_key_here"; npx vite
```

### 7. View the App
Once the command is running, the terminal will show a link (usually `http://localhost:5173`). Open that link in your browser.
